record.title: Rosie AI Pricing: Plans, Booking & Calendar Tiers
record.description: Review Rosie AI pricing and the difference between a booking link and a calendar appointment. Compare tier limits and the workflow with Revo.
record.lead: A texted scheduling link and a confirmed booking are different outcomes.
record.intro: Rosie’s tiers distinguish sending an appointment link from booking directly into a calendar. For a cleaning or repair business, that workflow difference may matter more than the entry monthly fee. Published by Revo. Official sources reviewed October 20, 2026; prices are dated US snapshots, not binding quotes or performance tests.

sections.title: Read the published offer in its own billing unit
paragraphs: Monthly Professional is $49 with 250 minutes and appointment-link texts. Scale is $149 with 1,000 minutes, direct calendar booking and live/warm transfers. Growth is $299 with 2,000 minutes and waterfall transfers. Annual billing is a separate selection. A current overage rate was not verified, so above-allowance totals are not calculated here.

sections.title: Match the service to your office decision
paragraphs: A cleaning office that only needs to send its online scheduling page can evaluate a different workflow from a team that needs the phone agent to reserve a slot during the call. In either case, check the final calendar state. An invitation to book should not be recorded internally as a confirmed appointment.

sections.title: Work through a home-service example
paragraphs: Use an ordinary week and a busy week to test the chosen tier. Include a caller who changes the requested service, an existing booking and a transfer when the first person is unavailable. Record whether the caller received a link, a confirmed slot or a callback request. Compare those outcomes against what your office will actually accept.

sections.title: Resolve these points before choosing
paragraphs: Use the same requested tasks in every proposal. A rate card describes an offer; a representative call test shows whether the configured flow does the work your office needs.
items: Confirm monthly versus annual billing before comparing totals.
Request the current extra-minute policy in writing.
Test slot duration and details after a direct booking.
Check the fallback rule when a transfer is unanswered.

sections.title: Compare with Revo using the same workload
paragraphs: Review Revo’s current plans and included minutes through the Pricing link. Compare the required answering, booking and team-handoff workflow with that exact plan, rather than assuming every feature is included in its entry tier. Record calls, handled minutes and required tasks together before comparing differently metered services.

For a practical shortlist, test a new inquiry, an appointment change and a request that needs a person. Check the final calendar or message, the handoff result and the usage charged. These are suggested evaluation steps, not customer results or a claim that either provider will complete every request.

faqs.q: Does the entry Rosie plan directly book a calendar slot?
faqs.a: The reviewed monthly comparison lists appointment-link texts on Professional and direct calendar booking on Scale. Confirm the selected tier and configuration.

faqs.q: What should a home-service office test?
faqs.a: Use a representative customer inquiry and verify the resulting message or appointment, routing behavior and billable usage. Do not equate answering a call with dispatching a technician.

record.takeaway: A texted scheduling link and a confirmed booking are different outcomes. Use the current written terms and a representative call flow before selecting a package.

sections.title: Separate inbound answering from the broader platform
paragraphs:
Broccoli’s [official homepage](https://www.broccoli.com/) names Inbound, Outbound, Speed to Lead, QA & Coaching, and AI Chat & Scheduling. It presents a home-service platform rather than one undifferentiated answering task. The [demo page](https://www.broccoli.com/demo) offers a route to see that platform; it does not establish a universal price for those components.

Ask which of those named areas your proposal actually includes. Do not assume they are separately priced, all bundled, or available under one fixed starting amount. A buyer needing only inbound coverage has a different comparison from a business purchasing outbound work, coaching and website conversations as well.

sections.title: Make the booking demonstration specific to your office
paragraphs:
The official site illustrates an inbound job booking associated with ServiceTitan. That is a vendor presentation, not proof of compatibility with your account, job types or booking rules. Ask the proposed provider to demonstrate the exact authorized action in an approved test environment.

Use a fictional request with a defined service, area and requested time. Then add an unavailable slot or a request that does not fit the business’s accepted work. Inspect what becomes a lead record, what becomes a confirmed booking and what remains with a staff owner. A natural conversation alone does not establish that the field-service record is correct.

Put the required software account, supported action and configuration owner in the quote notes. If any connection or authority is unresolved, record it as an open condition of the purchase instead of treating the demo illustration as acceptance evidence.

sections.title: Ask what the additional work includes
paragraphs:
For outbound and follow-up, identify the source of the work, trigger, retry limits and stop condition. Ask how attempts, connected conversations and any required staff work are measured. This is a question about the proposed service, not authorization to contact customers or a promise that a campaign meets every applicable requirement.

For speed-to-lead, identify the actual lead sources and records involved. Ask what happens when source details are missing or the same person contacts the business twice. A recognizable marketing-channel logo is not a completed reconciliation test.

For QA & Coaching, distinguish reviewing a conversation from assigning an unresolved case to a person who can act. For AI Chat & Scheduling, identify the channel, record and authorized calendar action separately from the telephone workflow. Request the scope and cost treatment of each requirement; do not invent extra fees or assume they are included.

sections.title: Use this module-and-quote worksheet
paragraphs:
Create one row for each required task. The fields below form an original worksheet you can reuse with the provider and your office. “Not required” is useful: it prevents a broad platform proposal from being compared with a narrower service as though both purchases were identical.

- Required task: [incoming request / supported booking / outbound follow-up / source response / call review / website conversation].
- Proposed scope: [named Broccoli module or written offer reference; included, excluded or unresolved].
- Authorized action: [record to create or change, applicable business rule and responsible owner].
- Acceptance evidence: [approved test case, observed result and unresolved exception].
- Implementation: [setup owner, prerequisites, staff work and future change responsibility].
- Commercial terms: [billing unit, allowance, recurring amount, one-time amount and excess-usage rule from the actual offer].
- Final decision: [required condition, person confirming it and date of the written answer].

sections.title: Keep implementation and ongoing ownership visible
paragraphs:
Ask who maintains the script, business knowledge, staff destinations and service rules after launch. If several locations or teams are involved, identify who approves changes and how an unavailable recipient is handled. A corrected operating rule should not depend on an informal promise that nobody owns.

Have the provider identify any relevant implementation work, recurring administration or usage conditions in writing. These are questions to resolve, not verified fee categories. We have not established a universal minimum, contract length, setup charge or onboarding duration for a Broccoli purchase.

sections.title: Use a narrower comparison when that is the real need
paragraphs:
Revo’s published [Services](/services) and [Pricing](/pricing) are relevant when the requirement is its supported inbound-answering, booking and handoff work. They do not establish an equivalent to Broccoli’s entire platform, outbound operation, QA/coaching or field-service actions.

Compare the required incoming-call outcome first. If the broader modules are necessary, keep them in a separate scope rather than declaring a phone-only offer a complete substitute. Without an applicable Broccoli price and matched responsibilities, this review cannot responsibly calculate a savings percentage or call either option the cheaper purchase.

If your requirement is inbound answering for a home-service business, review Revo’s current plans against the specific call-handling work you need. Confirm plan eligibility, connection and handoff before changing your live phone setup.

faqs.q: Does Broccoli publish a fixed starting price?
faqs.a: No numerical tariff was present on the homepage and demo page reviewed here. That is a limited source finding, not proof that no public price exists elsewhere.

faqs.q: Can I assume every named module is included?
faqs.a: No. Match the required work to the written offer. The website’s product names do not establish bundle or billing terms.

faqs.q: Are the website’s booking and revenue figures independent results?
faqs.a: They are vendor claims, not measurements established by this review. No such figures are used to predict your results.

record.title: Zanus AI Receptionist: Features & Buying Questions
record.description: Considering Zanus AI Phone? Review answering, staff roles and transfers for a residential service business, then compare the workflow with Revo.
record.lead: A small residential service business evaluating Zanus AI should identify the phone-handling purchase separately from the rest of its software catalog. An owner who needs callers answered while working on a job may not need every front-office, back-office or automated outreach function presented beside the receptionist.
record.intro: A small residential service business evaluating Zanus AI should identify the phone-handling purchase separately from the rest of its software catalog. An owner who needs callers answered while working on a job may not need every front-office, back-office or automated outreach function presented beside the receptionist.

sections.title: Identify AI Phone before comparing the larger catalog
paragraphs:
The [Zanus AI Phone page](https://zanusai.com/fo/ai-phone.html) describes incoming answering, approved business knowledge, department-specific instructions and transfers to staff. Its wider navigation also includes tools for quoting, contacts, marketing and other office work. A feature appearing elsewhere in the catalog does not establish its inclusion in the phone subscription you select.

The [Front Office pricing page](https://zanusai.com/fo/pricing.html) links to Front Office and AI Server products. The live price table was not available as readable text in this review, so this guide supplies no verified dollar tariff or allowance. Obtain the current selected offer directly rather than relying on an older comparison or a price attached to a different product.

Ask for the exact product, enabled functions, usage unit and recurring commitment in one proposal. Do not compare an entire office-software package with a reception plan solely because both pages mention answering calls.

sections.title: Distinguish a transfer recipient from a phone operator
paragraphs:
Zanus makes a useful product-specific distinction: a colleague receiving a forwarded call on an existing phone is different from an operator using a phone extension inside Front Office. Confirm which arrangement each person needs and how it affects the selected offer. This guide does not establish the current price of either arrangement.

Write down what your office needs after an AI conversation reaches its limit. Does an available employee receive a transfer, does the caller leave a request, or is another supported next step offered? Ask how the person accepts the handoff and what happens when they do not accept it. A destination number alone does not establish an available recipient.

For a service owner moving between jobs, the important demonstration is an unavailable person as well as a successful connection. Keep the office's callback responsibility visible instead of assuming the receptionist has resolved the customer's request.

sections.title: Complete this AI Phone purchase card
paragraphs:
Use the card to obtain evidence for the particular Zanus offer you are considering. These are original evaluation questions, not a list of functions guaranteed in every subscription.

| Requirement | What to confirm in the selected offer | Evidence to inspect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Business answers | Which approved source supplies a service or hours answer? | A sample answer and its accepted source |
| Incoming request | Which details are collected for a residential service inquiry? | The resulting record sent to the office |
| Appointment | Does the action request a time or confirm a supported booking? | The authoritative appointment record and confirmation boundary |
| Staff handoff | Is the recipient a forwarding target or an internal operator? | An accepted transfer and its accompanying context |
| Unavailable person | What happens when nobody accepts? | The supported fallback and named follow-up owner |
| Instruction change | Who approves an edit before it affects calls? | The accepted instruction and the observed caller response |
| Additional office work | Is quoting, outbound contact or another task separately enabled? | A specific scope, authority and charging definition |

Keep unanswered fields unresolved and use fictional requests for the demonstration.

sections.title: Test an unanswered question and a proposed rule change
paragraphs:
Zanus describes its phone product as working from approved knowledge and supporting staff handoff. Treat those descriptions as matters to verify in the account proposal and demonstration, not as proof that every answer will be correct.

Use a fictional homeowner asking about a service your business does not offer. Check whether the proposed workflow preserves that uncertainty and reaches the appropriate next step. Then provide an authorized change to ordinary office hours and ask how it becomes effective. Compare the caller's answer with the accepted instruction.

This is different from asking whether a website was imported. The business needs to know which information the active phone flow uses and who may change it. The separate [knowledge-base guide](/ai-answering-service/ai-receptionist-knowledge-base) explains the general source-review process; this purchase card connects that question to the selected Zanus phone arrangement and staff roles.

sections.title: Keep additional automation outside the reception comparison
paragraphs:
The AI Phone product page also advertises outbound and other office actions. Those can require a different task, permission and operating arrangement from receiving an incoming service inquiry. Do not assume they are needed, included or appropriate simply because they appear in the same product tour.

For example, a caller asking to discuss an existing estimate can be recorded for an authorized employee. That does not itself authorize a revised quote, a repeated outbound campaign or a change to a customer record. Identify which role would own any later action and verify the suitable arrangement separately.

This guide establishes no legal compliance conclusion for an outbound workflow, no technical connection to a particular field-service system and no on-premises phone deployment. It evaluates a reception purchase, not the full set of advertised office applications.

sections.title: Where Revo fits in the comparison
paragraphs:
Revo publishes AI answering, business-script intake, supported appointment booking and call summaries. Team transfers depend on the selected plan and supported configuration. Use [current Revo plans](/pricing) to verify the incoming-call scope your service business actually needs.

This page does not establish a Revo connection to Zanus, a Front Office operator panel, a back-office suite, outbound campaigns, automatic quote preparation or an on-premises server product. Compare the required reception outcomes and retained staff work, rather than treating all advertised software categories as equivalent.

sections.title: Questions before buying
paragraphs:
### Is every Zanus Front Office function part of AI Phone?

Do not infer that from shared navigation. Obtain the selected product and enabled functions in the actual proposal, including the usage and staff-role definitions.

### Does a staff mobile receiving transfers need the same arrangement as an internal operator?

Zanus describes them separately. Confirm how your selected offer handles each role and obtain the current terms rather than assuming the same entitlement or charge.

### Why are no Zanus prices listed here?

Its live pricing table was not available as readable text in this review. A current proposal is needed; this guide does not substitute a third party's historical prices or another product's terms.

[Review Revo's current plans](/pricing) with the completed purchase card and identify which reception tasks the supported setup can demonstrate.

record.intro: For a contractor buying AnswerMTI, the lowest monthly fee is only one part of the budget. Start with the minutes you expect the answering service to handle, then compare the allowance and additional-minute rate.

sections.title: Read the base fee together with the allowance
paragraphs: AnswerMTI’s advertised plans are:

| Plan | Monthly base | Included minutes | Additional minute |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Business | $47 | 0 | $1.37 |
| Growth | $177 | 125 | $1.30 |
| Premium | $296 | 225 | $1.28 |

Custom plans are available by quote. The Business base includes no minutes. The published offer describes month-to-month service with 30 days’ notice to stop. Confirm your account’s actual usage calculation and final charges before purchasing. These prices are a November 2, 2026 snapshot. [1]

sections.title: Estimate the work you would forward
paragraphs: Use the portion of your call log the service would actually receive. An office forwarding unanswered calls needs a different estimate from one forwarding its entire main line.

For a fictional HVAC shop, separate new service requests from existing-job questions and other calls. An estimate request may require more discussion than a quick callback message. A count of calls alone will not tell the office how many handled minutes to budget.

Ask AnswerMTI to explain rounding, transfers and any other time included in the usage calculation. Those questions help you turn a rate card into an account-specific estimate; they are not claims that each activity carries a separate fee.

sections.title: One illustrative budget, using the same minutes
paragraphs: At an assumed 100 billable minutes in one month, base-plus-minute arithmetic gives $184 for Business, $177 for Growth and $296 for Premium. That calculation applies the displayed rates and allowances only. It is not a quote or a customer result, and excludes any tax or other account-specific charge. [1]

This example shows why the lowest base fee need not give the lowest total for a particular workload. Repeat the comparison with your own expected minutes and ask for the proposed invoice treatment in writing.

sections.title: Match live answering to the contractor’s instructions
paragraphs: AnswerMTI’s contractor page describes live answering, custom scripts, caller information and contact with on-call staff. Agree on the work your account will perform before comparing it with an AI service. [2]

For an illustrative electrical office, decide which requests can receive a routine appointment and which need your team’s callback. Supply the approved questions and the contact who may authorize the next step. A caller’s urgent description should not become an arrival promise the office has not approved.
Ask the provider to demonstrate your proposed flow. Review what the office receives and what the caller is told. This is a suggested evaluation, not a claim that the service has been tested here.

sections.title: Compare with Revo’s AI reception
paragraphs: Revo describes AI reception, lead intake, routing and scheduling. That establishes a different answering model from staffed reception, without establishing identical task scope. Check the current Revo plan and supported setup against the same requests and expected workload. [3]

sections.title: Frequently asked questions
paragraphs:
Does the $47 plan include receptionist minutes?
No. The displayed Business plan has zero included minutes, with usage charged at its stated rate. [1]

Can a larger allowance be cheaper?
It can for a particular workload, as the illustrative calculation shows. Compare the full bill at your expected usage, then confirm the quote.

What should a contractor confirm before switching?
The tasks the provider may complete, how handled time is charged, the next step for callers and the account’s exit notice. Keep your office responsible for commitments it has not delegated.

# AnswerMTI Pricing: Minute Plans for Contractors

For a contractor buying AnswerMTI, the lowest monthly fee is only one part of the budget. Start with the minutes you expect the answering service to handle, then compare the allowance and additional-minute rate.

Published by Revo. Official sources checked November 2, 2026. Revo is not affiliated with AnswerMTI. This is a service-purchasing comparison, not a hands-on performance review.

## Read the base fee together with the allowance

AnswerMTI’s advertised plans are:

| Plan | Monthly base | Included minutes | Additional minute |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Business | $47 | 0 | $1.37 |
| Growth | $177 | 125 | $1.30 |
| Premium | $296 | 225 | $1.28 |

Custom plans are available by quote. The Business base includes no minutes. The published offer describes month-to-month service with 30 days’ notice to stop. Confirm your account’s actual usage calculation and final charges before purchasing. These prices are a November 2, 2026 snapshot. [1]

## Estimate the work you would forward

Use the portion of your call log the service would actually receive. An office forwarding unanswered calls needs a different estimate from one forwarding its entire main line.

For a fictional HVAC shop, separate new service requests from existing-job questions and other calls. An estimate request may require more discussion than a quick callback message. A count of calls alone will not tell the office how many handled minutes to budget.

Ask AnswerMTI to explain rounding, transfers and any other time included in the usage calculation. Those questions help you turn a rate card into an account-specific estimate; they are not claims that each activity carries a separate fee.

## One illustrative budget, using the same minutes

At an assumed 100 billable minutes in one month, base-plus-minute arithmetic gives $184 for Business, $177 for Growth and $296 for Premium. That calculation applies the displayed rates and allowances only. It is not a quote or a customer result, and excludes any tax or other account-specific charge. [1]

This example shows why the lowest base fee need not give the lowest total for a particular workload. Repeat the comparison with your own expected minutes and ask for the proposed invoice treatment in writing.

## Match live answering to the contractor’s instructions

AnswerMTI’s contractor page describes live answering, custom scripts, caller information and contact with on-call staff. Agree on the work your account will perform before comparing it with an AI service. [2]

For an illustrative electrical office, decide which requests can receive a routine appointment and which need your team’s callback. Supply the approved questions and the contact who may authorize the next step. A caller’s urgent description should not become an arrival promise the office has not approved.

Ask the provider to demonstrate your proposed flow. Review what the office receives and what the caller is told. This is a suggested evaluation, not a claim that the service has been tested here.

## Compare with Revo’s AI reception

Revo describes AI reception, lead intake, routing and scheduling. That establishes a different answering model from staffed reception, without establishing identical task scope. Check the current Revo plan and supported setup against the same requests and expected workload. [3]

## Frequently asked questions

Does the $47 plan include receptionist minutes?
No. The displayed Business plan has zero included minutes, with usage charged at its stated rate. [1]

Can a larger allowance be cheaper?
It can for a particular workload, as the illustrative calculation shows. Compare the full bill at your expected usage, then confirm the quote.

What should a contractor confirm before switching?
The tasks the provider may complete, how handled time is charged, the next step for callers and the account’s exit notice. Keep your office responsible for commitments it has not delegated.

record.description: Compare Marlie AI plans by actions per call, booking and transfer limits. Choose a workflow for your home-service office and review it alongside Revo.
record.lead: For a home-service office choosing Marlie AI, start with what one caller may need completed. A plan that takes a message can suit a different job from a plan that checks availability, books a visit and connects the caller to your team.
record.intro: For a home-service office choosing Marlie AI, start with what one caller may need completed. A plan that takes a message can suit a different job from a plan that checks availability, books a visit and connects the caller to your team.

sections.title: Match the plan to the actions you need
paragraphs: Marlie’s pricing page lists these monthly plans:

Plan       Price       Included minutes       Additional minute
Basic      $49         250                    $0.35
Standard   $99         500                    $0.35
Pro        $199        1,000                  $0.30
Premium    $399        2,000                  $0.25

Basic permits one action per call and excludes transfers. Standard allows up to three actions, adds calendar booking and rescheduling, and transfers to one number. Pro advertises unlimited actions, department routing, cancellation of bookings, custom fields and document uploads. Premium adds team-assisted multi-location setup and sequential staff ringing. These are dated advertised inclusions; confirm the applicable offer and how actions are counted. [1]

sections.title: Do not infer action counting from a feature list
paragraphs: Consider an illustrative air-conditioning office. One caller wants to move a visit, ask a question and speak with the office about the new time. Before choosing a plan, write down the sequence you expect and ask how the configured account handles it.

Do not decide on your own whether checking availability, changing a visit and sending a link count as one action or several. Ask Marlie to map the proposed sequence to its limit, including a failed attempt or a caller changing direction.

Then decide what should happen if the requested operation cannot finish. Your office might prefer a callback request to a partially completed appointment change. The right choice depends on your process, not simply on how many features appear in the plan.

sections.title: Check the home-service booking boundary
paragraphs: Marlie’s home-services page describes capturing job details and booking through field-service or calendar connections. It separates quoting a business-approved trip fee from committing to a repair price, and describes urgent notifications to the team. [2]

For your own evaluation, use a fictional caller who changes both the requested service and the preferred date. Check the final record your office would use. Have the office distinguish an appointment from a request still awaiting a person. Do not give a caller an arrival commitment that your business cannot support.

sections.title: Choose a transfer path your staff can answer
paragraphs: A fictional plumbing company might send every office question to one person. A larger shop may need different destinations during the day and after closing. Define who should receive each type of request and what the caller should hear if that person is unavailable.

Check those requirements against the chosen plan’s transfer provision. Ask for a demonstration of the unavailable-person path as well as the successful connection. A configured transfer is useful only if the resulting office process fits your staffing.

sections.title: Compare the required workflow with Revo
paragraphs: Revo’s public Services page describes AI reception, intake, routing and scheduling. It does not provide a matching Marlie-style action allowance. Confirm the supported operations for your Revo setup and use the current plan, rather than assuming matching limits or feature parity. [3]

sections.title: Frequently asked questions
paragraphs:
Is the entry plan suitable when callers need transfers?
The reviewed Basic plan excludes transfers. Match that requirement to a plan that explicitly includes it. [1]

Does an unlimited action allowance remove the minute allowance?
The reviewed plans list those as separate limits. Keep the minute budget in the comparison even when the action allowance is unlimited. [1]

What should I bring to a demonstration?
A short description of the caller’s request, the sequence your office wants completed and the person responsible when it cannot finish. That makes the plan choice specific to your business.

## Match the plan to the actions you need

Plan       Price       Included minutes       Additional minute
Basic      $49         250                    $0.35
Standard   $99         500                    $0.35

These are dated advertised inclusions; confirm the applicable offer and how actions are counted. [1]

## Do not infer action counting from a feature list

Consider an illustrative air-conditioning office. One caller wants to move a visit, ask a question and speak with the office about the new time. Before choosing a plan, write down the sequence you expect and ask how the configured account handles it.

Do not decide on your own whether checking availability, changing a visit and sending a link count as one action or several. Ask Marlie to map the proposed sequence to its limit, including a failed attempt or a caller changing direction.

Then decide what should happen if the requested operation cannot finish. Your office might prefer a callback request to a partially completed appointment change. The right choice depends on your process, not simply on how many features appear in the plan.
